claim: Proper mechanical stimulation can improve rotator cuff enthesis injury repair.
source: Proper mechanical stimulation can improve rotator cuff enthesis injury repair.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known fact that motivates the study.

claim: The underlying mechanism of mechanical stimulation promoting injury repair is still unknown.
source: However, the underlying mechanism of mechanical stimulation promoting injury repair is still unknown.
evidence: This is explicitly stated in the abstract as a knowledge gap.

claim: Prrx1+ cells are essential for murine rotator cuff enthesis development.
source: In this study, we found that Prrx1+ cell was essential for murine rotator cuff enthesis development identified by single-cell RNA sequence and involved in the injury repair.
evidence: This claim is supported by scRNA-seq data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Prrx1+ cells are involved in enthesis injury repair.
source: In this study, we found that Prrx1+ cell was essential for murine rotator cuff enthesis development identified by single-cell RNA sequence and involved in the injury repair.
evidence: This is supported by lineage tracing experiments shown in the manuscript.

claim: Proper mechanical stimulation promotes the migration of Prrx1+ cells to enhance enthesis injury repair.
source: Proper mechanical stimulation could promote the migration of Prrx1+ cells to enhance enthesis injury repair.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data showing increased Prrx1+ cell migration with mechanical stimulation.

claim: TGF-β signaling plays an essential role in mediating mechanical stimulation signaling transmission.
source: Meantime, TGF-β signaling and primary cilia played an essential role in mediating mechanical stimulation signaling transmission.
evidence: This is supported by experiments using TGF-β neutralizing antibody and ELISA measurements.

claim: Primary cilia play an essential role in mediating mechanical stimulation signaling transmission.
source: Meantime, TGF-β signaling and primary cilia played an essential role in mediating mechanical stimulation signaling transmission.
evidence: This is supported by experiments using Ift88 knockout mice.

claim: Proper mechanical stimulation enhances the release of active TGF-β1 to promote migration of Prrx1+ cells.
source: Proper mechanical stimulation enhanced the release of active TGF-β1 to promote migration of Prrx1+ cells.
evidence: This is supported by ELISA data showing increased TGF-β1 concentration with mechanical stimulation.

claim: Inhibition of TGF-β signaling eliminates the stimulatory effect of mechanical stimulation on Prrx1+ cell migration.
source: Inhibition of TGF-β signaling eliminated the stimulatory effect of mechanical stimulation on Prrx1+ cell migration and enthesis injury repair.
evidence: This is supported by experiments using TGF-β neutralizing antibody (ab64715).

claim: Inhibition of TGF-β signaling eliminates the stimulatory effect of mechanical stimulation on enthesis injury repair.
source: Inhibition of TGF-β signaling eliminated the stimulatory effect of mechanical stimulation on Prrx1+ cell migration and enthesis injury repair.
evidence: This is supported by histological and mechanical testing data from mice treated with TGF-β neutralizing antibody.

claim: Knockdown of Pallidin inhibits TGF-βR2 translocation to the primary cilia.
source: In addition, knockdown of Pallidin to inhibit TGF-βR2 translocation to the primary cilia or deletion of Ift88 in Prrx1+ cells also restrained the mechanics-induced Prrx1+ cells migration.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data showing reduced ciliary TGF-βR2 after Pallidin knockdown.

claim: Knockdown of Pallidin restrains mechanics-induced Prrx1+ cell migration.
source: In addition, knockdown of Pallidin to inhibit TGF-βR2 translocation to the primary cilia or deletion of Ift88 in Prrx1+ cells also restrained the mechanics-induced Prrx1+ cells migration.
evidence: This is supported by scratch assay and transwell assay data.

claim: Deletion of Ift88 in Prrx1+ cells restrains mechanics-induced Prrx1+ cell migration.
source: In addition, knockdown of Pallidin to inhibit TGF-βR2 translocation to the primary cilia or deletion of Ift88 in Prrx1+ cells also restrained the mechanics-induced Prrx1+ cells migration.
evidence: This is supported by lineage tracing and migration assay data from Ift88 knockout mice.

claim: Mechanical stimulation increases the release of active TGF-β1 and enhances mobilization of Prrx1+ cells to promote enthesis injury repair via ciliary TGF-β signaling.
source: These findings suggested that mechanical stimulation could increase the release of active TGF-β1 and enhance the mobilization of Prrx1+ cells to promote enthesis injury repair via ciliary TGF-β signaling.
evidence: This is the main conclusion supported by multiple experiments throughout the manuscript.

claim: Rotator cuff tear is common in modern sports activity.
source: Rotator cuff (RC) tear is common in modern sports activity, which often causes persistent shoulder pain and dysfunction (Meislin et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Meislin et al., 2005.

claim: Rotator cuff tear often causes persistent shoulder pain and dysfunction.
source: Rotator cuff (RC) tear is common in modern sports activity, which often causes persistent shoulder pain and dysfunction (Meislin et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Meislin et al., 2005.

claim: Surgical repair has been a well-established and commonly accepted treatment for severe RC tear.
source: Surgical repair has been a well-established and commonly accepted treatment for severe RC tear, especially when conservative treatment fails (Galatz et al., 2001; Chung et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Galatz et al., 2001 and Chung et al., 2013.

claim: Approximately 450,000 patients were accepted RC repairs surgery annually in the United States.
source: It has been reported that approximately 450,000 patients were accepted RC repairs surgery annually in the United States (Thigpen et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Thigpen et al., 2016.

claim: The results of surgical repair are not always satisfactory.
source: However, the results of surgical repair are not always satisfactory (Lee et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lee et al., 2020.

claim: Structural failure of the RC repair ranges from 16% to 94%.
source: Previous studies have shown structural failure of the RC repair ranging from 16% to 94%, with poor outcomes associated with failed microstructure regeneration of RC enthesis (Thigpen et al., 2016; Hein et al., 2015; Galatz et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Thigpen et al., 2016; Hein et al., 2015; Galatz et al., 2004.

claim: Poor outcomes are associated with failed microstructure regeneration of RC enthesis.
source: Previous studies have shown structural failure of the RC repair ranging from 16% to 94%, with poor outcomes associated with failed microstructure regeneration of RC enthesis (Thigpen et al., 2016; Hein et al., 2015; Galatz et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Thigpen et al., 2016; Hein et al., 2015; Galatz et al., 2004.

claim: The RC enthesis consists of four distinct yet continuous tissue layers: bone, calcified cartilage, uncalcified cartilage, and tendon.
source: Histologically, the RC enthesis has been consisted of four distinct yet continuous tissue layers: bone, calcified cartilage, uncalcified cartilage, and tendon.
evidence: This is established knowledge about enthesis structure.

claim: The enthesis structure can subtly transfer force from muscle to bone.
source: This kind of structure can subtly transfer force from muscle to bone, while enthesis functional injury repair remains an insurmountable challenge in sports medicine.Chen et al., 2019
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Chen et al., 2019.

claim: Enthesis functional injury repair remains an insurmountable challenge in sports medicine.
source: This kind of structure can subtly transfer force from muscle to bone, while enthesis functional injury repair remains an insurmountable challenge in sports medicine.Chen et al., 2019
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Chen et al., 2019.

claim: Moderate mechanical load is essential for enthesis development and maintenance.
source: Moderate mechanical load is essential for enthesis development and maintenance (Thampatty and Wang, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Thampatty and Wang, 2018.

claim: The clinical application of mechanobiological principles following enthesis injury forms the basic rehabilitation protocols.
source: Meanwhile, the clinical application of mechanobiological principles following enthesis injury forms the basic rehabilitation protocols (Thomopoulos et al., 2007; Galloway et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Thomopoulos et al., 2007 and Galloway et al., 2013.

claim: There is a debate about the initiating time and strength of mechanical stimulation during enthesis healing procedure.
source: However, there is a debate about the initiating time and strength of mechanical stimulation during enthesis healing procedure (Chang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Chang et al., 2015.

claim: A traditional rehabilitation program after RC repair suggests delaying mechanical exercise (immobilization for about 6 weeks).
source: In clinical treatment, a traditional rehabilitation program after RC repair has been suggested to delay mechanical exercise (immobilization for about 6 weeks) (Keener et al., 2014), while an accelerated protocol suggests that an immediate exercise with limited range of motion would be better for tendon healing (Lee et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Keener et al., 2014.

claim: An accelerated protocol suggests that immediate exercise with limited range of motion would be better for tendon healing.
source: In clinical treatment, a traditional rehabilitation program after RC repair has been suggested to delay mechanical exercise (immobilization for about 6 weeks) (Keener et al., 2014), while an accelerated protocol suggests that an immediate exercise with limited range of motion would be better for tendon healing (Lee et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lee et al., 2012.

claim: Zhang et al adopted treadmill training at postoperative day 7 on murine enthesis injury repair model and found that mechanical stimulation could improve enthesis fibrocartilage and bone regeneration.
source: Zhang et al adopted treadmill training at postoperative day 7 on murine enthesis injury repair model and found that mechanical stimulation could improve enthesis fibrocartilage and bone regeneration and obtained better mechanical parameters (Zhang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Zhang et al., 2021.

claim: Zhang et al obtained better mechanical parameters with treadmill training.
source: Zhang et al adopted treadmill training at postoperative day 7 on murine enthesis injury repair model and found that mechanical stimulation could improve enthesis fibrocartilage and bone regeneration and obtained better mechanical parameters (Zhang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Zhang et al., 2021.

claim: There is a correlation between appropriate mechanical stimulation and high quality of enthesis healing.
source: Although we know that there is a correlation between appropriate mechanical stimulation and high quality of enthesis healing, the uncovering mechanism is poorly understood.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a knowledge gap.

claim: The mechanism of how appropriate mechanical stimulation improves enthesis healing is poorly understood.
source: Although we know that there is a correlation between appropriate mechanical stimulation and high quality of enthesis healing, the uncovering mechanism is poorly understood.
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap.

claim: Soluble inflammatory mediators bind to cell surface or cytoplasmic receptors during wound regeneration.
source: During the wound regeneration procedure, soluble inflammatory mediators bind to cell surface or cytoplasmic receptors, and lead to recruitment of immune cells, stem cells and tissue-resident cells by activating signaling cascades (Wynn and Vannella, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Wynn and Vannella, 2016.

claim: Inflammatory mediators lead to recruitment of immune cells, stem cells and tissue-resident cells by activating signaling cascades.
source: During the wound regeneration procedure, soluble inflammatory mediators bind to cell surface or cytoplasmic receptors, and lead to recruitment of immune cells, stem cells and tissue-resident cells by activating signaling cascades (Wynn and Vannella, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Wynn and Vannella, 2016.

claim: Stem cells are essential for enthesis regeneration.
source: As we known, stem cells are essential for enthesis regeneration.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Prrx1 is a paired-related homeobox gene that is expressed in undifferentiated mesenchymal stem cells in the developing limb buds.
source: Prrx1 is a paired-related homeobox gene that is expressed in undifferentiated mesenchymal stem cells in the developing limb buds (Kawanami et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kawanami et al., 2009.

claim: Prrx1 transgene marks osteochondral progenitors in the periosteum.
source: A previous study showed that Prrx1 transgene marked osteochondral progenitors in the periosteum and played an essential role in skeletal development (Ouyang et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Ouyang et al., 2014.

claim: Prrx1 plays an essential role in skeletal development.
source: A previous study showed that Prrx1 transgene marked osteochondral progenitors in the periosteum and played an essential role in skeletal development (Ouyang et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Ouyang et al., 2014.

claim: Mice lacking Prrx1 transgenes show craniofacial defect, limb shortening, and incompletely penetrant Spina bifida.
source: Mice lacking Prrx1 transgenes would show craniofacial defect, limb shortening, and incompletely penetrant Spina bifida (Martin and Olson, 2000).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Martin and Olson, 2000.

claim: Prrx1+ cells are indispensable stem cell lineage for the musculoskeletal system.
source: Considering Prrx1+ cells are indispensable stem cell lineage for the musculoskeletal system, we want to specificlly reveal the role of Prrx1+ cells in enthesis injury repair and uncover the mechanism of mechanical stimulation on improving enthesis injury repair in this study.
evidence: This is stated as a premise based on prior knowledge.

claim: Primary cilia is an antenna-like sensory organelle based on immotile microtube.
source: Primary cilia is an antenna-like sensory organelle based on immotile microtube, and present on nearly every cell type, including mesenchymal stem cells, endothelial cells (ECs), epithelial cells, fibroblasts, and other cells in vertebrates (Nauli et al., 2008; Bowie and Goetz, 2020; Hilgendorf et al., 2019; Vion et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Nauli et al., 2008; Bowie and Goetz, 2020; Hilgendorf et al., 2019; Vion et al., 2018.

claim: Primary cilia are present on nearly every cell type in vertebrates.
source: Primary cilia is an antenna-like sensory organelle based on immotile microtube, and present on nearly every cell type, including mesenchymal stem cells, endothelial cells (ECs), epithelial cells, fibroblasts, and other cells in vertebrates (Nauli et al., 2008; Bowie and Goetz, 2020; Hilgendorf et al., 2019; Vion et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Nauli et al., 2008; Bowie and Goetz, 2020; Hilgendorf et al., 2019; Vion et al., 2018.

claim: Primary cilia contains a distinct subset of receptors and other proteins.
source: Primary cilia contains a distinct subset of receptors and other proteins, which make it a sophisticated signaling center functioning as mechanosensor and chemosensation (Nauli et al., 2003; Hua and Ferland, 2018; Guemez-Gamboa et al., 2014; Anvarian et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Nauli et al., 2003; Hua and Ferland, 2018; Guemez-Gamboa et al., 2014; Anvarian et al., 2019.

claim: Primary cilia functions as mechanosensor and chemosensation.
source: Primary cilia contains a distinct subset of receptors and other proteins, which make it a sophisticated signaling center functioning as mechanosensor and chemosensation (Nauli et al., 2003; Hua and Ferland, 2018; Guemez-Gamboa et al., 2014; Anvarian et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Nauli et al., 2003; Hua and Ferland, 2018; Guemez-Gamboa et al., 2014; Anvarian et al., 2019.

claim: Translocating receptors to the primary cilia can enhance signaling transmission.
source: Previous study also found that translocating receptors to the primary cilia could enhance the signaling transmission (Zheng et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Zheng et al., 2018.

claim: Defect or dysfunction of primary cilia leads to severe disorders known as ciliopathies.
source: Defect or dysfunction of primary cilia could lead to severe disorders of the body, which is known as ciliopathies, such as polycystic kidney disease, primary ciliary dyskinesia, retinopathies, combined developmental deficiencies, and other sensory disorders (Bisgrove and Yost, 2006; Miyamoto et al., 2020; Bergmann et al., 2018; May-Simera et al., 2018; Robichaux et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bisgrove and Yost, 2006; Miyamoto et al., 2020; Bergmann et al., 2018; May-Simera et al., 2018; Robichaux et al., 2019.

claim: Genetic deletion of Ift88 decreases load-induced bone formation.
source: Genetic deletion of Ift88, an encoded protein closely associated with cilia formation and maintenance, could decrease the load-induced bone formation (Moore et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Moore et al., 2018.

claim: Primary cilia is a hub for transducing biophysical and hedgehog signals to regulate tendon enthesis formation and adaptation to loading.
source: At the same time, the primary cilia is a hub for transducing biophysical and hedgehog signals to regulate tendon enthesis formation and adaptation to loading (Yuan and Yang, 2015; Fang et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Yuan and Yang, 2015 and Fang et al., 2020.

claim: 21,532 high-quality single-cell transcriptomic data were obtained from murine enthesis at E15.5, P7, and P28.
source: After sequencing and data quality processing, we got high-quality transcriptomic data from 21,532 single-cells, including 8,919 E15.5 cells, 7489 P7 cells, and 5124 P28 cells.
evidence: This is directly stated in the results section describing the scRNA-seq data.

claim: 23 major cell populations were identified in the developing enthesis by Seurat analysis.
source: We carried out unbiased clustering analysis for all single-cells and identified 23 major cell populations in the developing enthesis by Seurat analysis (Figure 1c, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by the UMAP plot in Figure 1c showing 23 clusters.

claim: 15 clusters were annotated into distinct cell types or states based on differential gene expression analysis.
source: Through differential gene expression analysis, we annotated 15 clusters into distinct cell types or states based on the expression of genes uniquely or in combinations represented individual cluster identities (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by the gene expression data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Seven enthesis related clusters were identified: BMSCs, Fibroblastic cells, Tenocytes, Chondrocytes, Proliferative stromal cells, Osteoblast/Osteocyte (OB/Ocy), Lepr+ cells.
source: Feature plot showed the canonical marker genes, which enriched in seven enthesis related clusters: BMSCs, Fibroblastic cells, Tenocytes, Chondrocytes, Proliferative stromal cells, Osteoblast/Osteocyte (OB/Ocy), Lepr+ cells (Figure 1d).
evidence: This is supported by the feature plot in Figure 1d showing marker gene expression.

claim: The rate of OB/Ocy and Lepr+ cells increased significantly in P7 and P28.
source: Cell fraction related to enthesis development showed that the rate of OB/Ocy and Lepr+ cells increased significantly in P7 and P28, which was consistent with the enthesis mineralization procedure.
evidence: This is supported by the cell composition data shown in Figure 1e.

claim: Chondrocytes were high in E15.5, P7 and decreased significantly in P28.
source: At the same time, chondrocytes were high in E15.5, P7 and decreased significantly in P28 (Figure 1e).
evidence: This is supported by the cell composition data shown in Figure 1e.

claim: The maturation of enthesis is highly correlated with osteochondrogenesis procedure.
source: These data suggested that the maturation of enthesis was higly correlated with osteochondrogenesis procedure.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the cell composition changes during development.

claim: 5,607 Prrx1+ cells from mouse enthesis (E15.5, P7, and P28) were grouped into five distinct clusters.
source: To examing the role of of Prrx1+ cells in enthesis development, 5,607 Prrx1+ cells from mouse enthesis (E15.5, P7, and P28) were analyzed and were grouped into five distinct clusters: BMSCs, Fibroblastic cells, Tenocytes, Chondrocytes, and Lepr+ cells.
evidence: This is directly stated in the results section.

claim: Prrx1 expression was relatively high in E15.5 and P7, while decreased significantly in P28.
source: Prrx1 expression was relatively high in E15.5 and P7, while decreased significantly in P28 (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is supported by the expression data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: Prrx1+ cells are highly involved in enthesis development via differentiating into tenocytes, osteoblasts/osteocytes or chondrocytes.
source: These results indicated that Prrx1+ cells were highly involved in enthesis development via differentiating into tenocytes, osteoblasts/osteocytes or chondrocytes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the pseudotime trajectory analysis shown in Figure 2b and 2c.

claim: Ribonucleoprotein complex biogenesis and assembly activities were significantly upregulated in Prrx1+ cells at E15.5.
source: The results showed that the ribonucleoprotein complex biogenesis and assembly activities were significantly upregulated in E15.5, while extracellular matrix organization activities in P7 and ossification activities in P28.
evidence: This is supported by the GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 2d.

claim: Extracellular matrix organization activities were upregulated in Prrx1+ cells at P7.
source: The results showed that the ribonucleoprotein complex biogenesis and assembly activities were significantly upregulated in E15.5, while extracellular matrix organization activities in P7 and ossification activities in P28.
evidence: This is supported by the GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 2d.

claim: Ossification activities were upregulated in Prrx1+ cells at P28.
source: The results showed that the ribonucleoprotein complex biogenesis and assembly activities were significantly upregulated in E15.5, while extracellular matrix organization activities in P7 and ossification activities in P28.
evidence: This is supported by the GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 2d.

claim: Prrx1+ cells are potential reliable progenitors for enthesis development.
source: These data suggested that Prrx1+ cells could be the potential reliable progenitors for enthesis development.
evidence: This is an inference based on the GO enrichment and trajectory analysis.

claim: Active Prrx1+ cells were abundant on the peripheral humeral head in young mice and decreased markedly during late adulthood.
source: We found that active Prrx1+ cells (high expression of GFP) were abundant on the peripheral humeral head in young mice and decreased markedly during late adulthood (Figure 3a).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3a and 3b.

claim: Active Prrx1+ cells were present during the early postnatal period and decreased significantly with age.
source: At the enthesis, we found active Prrx1+ cells were present during the early postnatal period, while they decreased significantly with age, then, disappeared and were confined within the perichondrium at adulthood (Figure 3b and c).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3b and quantification in Figure 3c.

claim: Most cells in the enthesis originated from Prrx1+ cells at the 2 W-12W group.
source: We found that most of the cells in the enthesis originated from Prrx1+ cells at the 2 W-12W group.
evidence: This is supported by lineage tracing data shown in Figure 3e and 3f.

claim: Prrx1+ cell involvement in enthesis development decreased significantly at the 4 W-12W group.
source: At the same time, this involvement decreased significantly at the 4 W-12W group and disappeared at the 8 W-12W group.
evidence: This is supported by lineage tracing data shown in Figure 3e and 3f.

claim: Prrx1+ cell involvement in enthesis development disappeared at the 8 W-12W group.
source: At the same time, this involvement decreased significantly at the 4 W-12W group and disappeared at the 8 W-12W group.
evidence: This is supported by lineage tracing data shown in Figure 3e and 3f.

claim: Prrx1+ cells participated in the development of enthesis, including the continuous four gradient layer structure: bone, calcified fibrocartilage, uncalcified fibrocartilage, and tendon.
source: Prrx1+ cells participated in the development of enthesis, including the continuous four gradient layer structure: bone, calcified fibrocartilage, uncalcified fibrocartilage, and tendon (Figure 3e and f).
evidence: This is supported by lineage tracing data shown in Figure 3e and 3f.

claim: Prrx1+ cells have stem-like cell phenotype.
source: We have isolated the Prrx1+ cells and verified that it has the stem-like cell phenotype (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry and differentiation assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Prrx1+ cell is a vital subpopulation of mesenchymal stem cells for enthesis development.
source: These finding suggested that Prrx1+ cell was a vital subpopulation of mesenchymal stem cells for enthesis development.
evidence: This is an inference based on the lineage tracing and characterization data.

claim: Prrx1+ cells were activated and migrated from the surrounding area to the injury site to participate in enthesis healing.
source: We found that Prrx1+ cells were activated and migrated from the surrounding area to the injury site to participate in the enthesis healing via differentiating into osteocytes or chondrocytes (Figure 3h and i).
evidence: This is supported by lineage tracing data in the injury model shown in Figure 3h and 3i.

claim: Prrx1+ cells participate in enthesis healing via differentiating into osteocytes or chondrocytes.
source: We found that Prrx1+ cells were activated and migrated from the surrounding area to the injury site to participate in the enthesis healing via differentiating into osteocytes or chondrocytes (Figure 3h and i).
evidence: This is supported by lineage tracing data in the injury model shown in Figure 3h and 3i.

claim: Treadmill training with 20 min per day showed better tissue maturation and collagen arrangement.
source: We found that treadmill training with 20 min per day showed better tissue maturation, collagen arrangement (Figure 4b), higher histological scores (Figure 4c), and more fibrocartilage regeneration (Figure 4d).
evidence: This is supported by histological data shown in Figure 4b, 4c, and 4d.

claim: Treadmill training with 20 min per day resulted in higher histological scores.
source: We found that treadmill training with 20 min per day showed better tissue maturation, collagen arrangement (Figure 4b), higher histological scores (Figure 4c), and more fibrocartilage regeneration (Figure 4d).
evidence: This is supported by histological scoring data shown in Figure 4c.

claim: Treadmill training with 20 min per day resulted in more fibrocartilage regeneration.
source: We found that treadmill training with 20 min per day showed better tissue maturation, collagen arrangement (Figure 4b), higher histological scores (Figure 4c), and more fibrocartilage regeneration (Figure 4d).
evidence: This is supported by fibrocartilage thickness measurements shown in Figure 4d.

claim: The best mechanical results of RC occurred at the group receiving 20 min treadmill training per day.
source: The best mechanical results of RC have also occurred at the group receiving 20 min treadmill training per day (Figure 4e).
evidence: This is supported by mechanical testing data shown in Figure 4e.

claim: Proper mechanical stimulation improves enthesis healing.
source: These results indicated that proper mechanical stimulation could improve enthesis healing.
evidence: This is an inference based on the histological and mechanical testing data from Figure 4.

claim: Prrx1+ cells were absent at the enthesis in adult mice.
source: We found that Prrx1+ cells were absent at the enthesis in adult mice (Figure 5b).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5b.

claim: Prrx1+ cells migrated from nearby tissue to the healing area at 2 weeks after surgery.
source: Prrx1+ cells could migrate from the nearby tissue to the healing area at 2 weeks after surgery (Figure 5b).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5b.

claim: 10 min and 20 min treadmill training significantly enhanced the migration of Prrx1+ cells to the healing area.
source: The 10 min and 20 min treadmill training could significantly enhance the migration of Prrx1+ cells to the healing area compared with the group without treadmill training.
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 5c.

claim: Excessive treadmill training decreased the migration of Prrx1+ cells to the healing area.
source: Excessive treadmill training decreased the migration of Prrx1+ cells to the healing area (Figure 5c).
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 5c.

claim: TGF-β1 can recruit mesenchymal stem cells to maintain the balance of bone resorption and formation.
source: Previous report showed that TGF-β1 can recruit mesenchymal stem cells to maintain the balance of bone resorption and formation (Tang et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Tang et al., 2009.

claim: Prrx1+ cells were highly responsive to TGF-β at P7.
source: The GO analysis found that Prrx1+ cells were highly responded to TGF-β at P7, when enthesis initial mineralization began.
evidence: This is based on GO analysis of the scRNA-seq data.

claim: Active TGF-β1 concentration increased and reached the peak at 2 weeks after surgery.
source: We found that active TGF-β1 concentration increased and reached the peak at 2 weeks after surgery.
evidence: This is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 6b.

claim: Active TGF-β1 concentration returned to basal level at 10 weeks after surgery.
source: Then, it returned to its basal level at 10 weeks.
evidence: This is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 6b.

claim: Mechanical stimulation stimulates the release of active TGF-β1 during the repair procedure.
source: Mechanical stimulation could stimulate the release of active TGF-β1 during the repair procedure.
evidence: This is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 6b.

claim: There is an active TGF-β1 concentration gradient between enthesis and nearby perichondrium.
source: Meantime, there is an active TGF-β1 concentration gradient between enthesis and nearby perichondrium (Figure 6b).
evidence: This is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 6b.

claim: Groups with TGF-β1 neutralizing antibody had lower failure load and stiffness than groups without antibody.
source: The mechanical test showed that groups with ab64715 had lower failure load and stiffness than other groups without ab64715 at each time point (p < 0.05 for all) (Figure 6e).
evidence: This is supported by mechanical testing data shown in Figure 6e.

claim: Treadmill training enhances Prrx1+ cell migration to the healing area.
source: We found that treadmill training could enhance Prrx1+ cells to the healing area and this effect could be eliminated by the treatment with TGF-β1 neutralizing antibody (Figure 6f).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6f.

claim: TGF-β1 neutralizing antibody eliminates the effect of treadmill training on Prrx1+ cell migration.
source: We found that treadmill training could enhance Prrx1+ cells to the healing area and this effect could be eliminated by the treatment with TGF-β1 neutralizing antibody (Figure 6f).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6f.

claim: Mechanical stimulation cannot independently enhance Prrx1+ cell migration ability.
source: We found that mechanical stimulation could not indipendently enhance the Prrx1+ cell migration ability.
evidence: This is supported by in vitro scratch and transwell assay data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: TGF-β1 improves Prrx1+ cell migration ability.
source: At the same time, TGF-β1 could improve its migration ability, and this effect could be significantly stimulated by mechanical stimulation (Figure 6—figure supplement 1b, c, d).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro scratch and transwell assay data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Mechanical stimulation significantly enhances the effect of TGF-β1 on Prrx1+ cell migration.
source: At the same time, TGF-β1 could improve its migration ability, and this effect could be significantly stimulated by mechanical stimulation (Figure 6—figure supplement 1b, c, d).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro scratch and transwell assay data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: pSmad2/3 was activated during the TGF-β1 and mechanical stimulation process.
source: Western blot showed that pSmad2/3 was activated during this process (Figure 6—figure supplement 1e, f).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1e and 1f.

claim: Treadmill training mobilizes Prrx1+ cells to enhance enthesis injury repair mainly by mediating the release of active TGF-β1.
source: These results indicated that treadmill training mobilised Prrx1+ cells to enhance enthesis injury repair mainly by mediating the release of active TGF-β1.
evidence: This is an inference based on the combined in vivo and in vitro data.

claim: Conditional ablation of Ift88 in Prrx1+ cells significantly damaged the primary cilia.
source: Results showed that conditional ablation of Ift88 in Prrx1+ cells significantly damaged the primary cilia (Figure 7a and b).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 7a and quantification in Figure 7b.

claim: Without primary cilia, mechanical stimulation cannot enhance the migration of Prrx1+ cells to the healing area.
source: Without the primary cilia, mechanical stimulation could not enhance the migration of Prrx1+ cells to the healing area (Figure 7c and d).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 7c and quantification in Figure 7d.
